Works with yours. kube-noob is a Kubernetes, OpenShift, ROSA HCP, Helm and RHACS/StackRox expert in a box: audit rules, read-only-first playbooks, cited docs and graded exercises. Claude, OpenShift Lightspeed or any MCP client calls it as tools; the CLI runs it with no AI at all. Two questions other tools leave unanswered, offline, from files you already have: kube-noob examples copy examples kube-noob policy reach --from web/frontend --to shop/payments --port 9090 -f examples/netpol-admin-tiers.yaml kube-noob policy explain -f examples/denial-multi.txt Before examples copy (from 0.9.3), download the two files: curl --create-dirs -fsSL -o examples/netpol-admin-tiers.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kube-noob/kube-noob/main/examples/netpol-admin-tiers.yaml -o examples/denial-multi.txt https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kube-noob/kube-noob/main/examples/denial-multi.txt Which policy governs this traffic? AdminNetworkPolicy → NetworkPolicy → BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy , in cluster order, naming the tier, policy and rule that decided. A checker reading NetworkPolicy alone gives a wrong answer wherever a platform team set cluster-wide guardrails, not a narrower one. Which system denied this pod? One pass across Pod Security, SCC, Kyverno, Gatekeeper, VAP and RHACS, with the smallest fix. reach exits 1 when denied; both say what they could not determine. Also: 100 rules with strict schemas and 9 red-team scenarios; 67 offline playbooks, read-only steps first; must-gathers triaged into a case draft that says what could not be read; OpenShift bugs with fix versions; hardened manifests and admission policies; 6 tracks, 22 lessons. kube-noob gate puts any of it in CI with SARIF and one exception list, and a design request runs the 7-step protocol. All of it: use-cases.md . Who does the thinking You use Who answers What leaves your machine The Claude plugin, or any MCP client That client's model, calling kube-noob's tools What you send that client; kube-noob sends nothing The CLI kube-noob's rules, no model Nothing kube-noob ask (optional) A model you configure Your question, to that model only Quick start brew tap kube-noob/kube-noob https://github.com/kube-noob/kube-noob brew trust --formula kube-noob/kube-noob/kube-noob brew install kube-noob kube-noob demo --list kube-noob audit -f your-manifests/ --platform openshift --version 4.22 kube-noob insight 'paste anything' kube-noob doctor No Homebrew: uv tool install kube-noob (Python 3.11.4+); install help . Use with Claude or any MCP client Claude plugin, in Claude Code (needs uv ): /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob /plugin install kube-noob@kube-noob Desktop, claude.ai, the plugin directory, Agent Skill: install.md . Any MCP client: {"mcpServers": {"kube-noob": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["--from", "kube-noob==0.11.1", "kube-noob", "mcp"]}}} Run on OpenShift As a token-protected service, loopback-only sidecar or Lightspeed tool: docs/openshift.md . The chart ships NetworkPolicies, written for restricted-v2 . Safe by default Off until you turn it on: web lookups, live cluster access (read-only, never Secrets), and any model at all. An admin offline: true lock overrides every one of them and nothing later in the config chain can lift it. Config never comes from the current directory. kube-noob doctor shows what the process can reach and exits 1 if the configuration contradicts the lock; every key is in kube-noob.example.yaml , and the generated safety contract lists what each capability tier can do. Docs Everything is at kube-noob.com , and in docs/ : use cases , architecture , accuracy , guidance , learning , privacy , security , contributing , limits , roadmap , maintenance , governance . Homebrew and uv bring their own Python (uv downloads one when yours is too old), and pipx installed with Homebrew uses Homebrew's. Method Commands Upgrade Homebrew (Apple silicon macOS, Linux) brew tap kube-noob/kube-noob https://github.com/kube-noob/kube-noob , then brew trust --formula kube-noob/kube-noob/kube-noob , then brew install kube-noob brew update && brew upgrade kube-noob uv (downloads a Python if yours is too old) uv tool install kube-noob uv tool upgrade kube-noob pipx pipx install kube-noob pipx upgrade kube-noob pip, in a virtual environment python3.13 -m venv ~/.venvs/kube-noob , then ~/.venvs/kube-noob/bin/pip install kube-noob ~/.venvs/kube-noob/bin/pip install -U kube-noob Container podman run --rm ghcr.io/kube-noob/kube-noob:0.11 --version pull the new tag Claude Code plugin /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob , then /plugin install kube-noob@kube-noob /plugin marketplace update kube-noob Claude Code plugin, CLI-driven /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob , then /plugin install kube-noob-skills@kube-noob , plus the CLI by any method above /plugin marketplace update kube-noob kube-noob-skills is the same seven skills with no MCP server and no code in the plugin at all . Its skills run the kube-noob CLI you installed, through Claude's Bash tool, with --format json . It exists because the Claude plugin directory accepts a plugin carrying a local MCP server only from a Verified organization, and there is no way to apply to become one. See which install, and what can run . Which install, and what can run kube-noob is one engine. What changes from one place to another is how Claude, or you, reach it. Where you are What you install What can run Claude Code, from this repository's marketplace /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob , then /plugin install kube-noob@kube-noob The full plugin: its own stdio MCP server, bundled as readable source and started with uv run --frozen , and seven skills that call its tools. Needs uv Claude Code, from the Claude plugin directory (once kube-noob-skills is listed) kube-noob-skills , and the CLI: pipx install 'kube-noob>=0.9.3' (0.9.3 is the first release the skills work with) The seven skills check kube-noob --version , then run the CLI through the Bash tool on a private folder, offline, under your permission settings, with KUBE_NOOB_FOR_MODEL=1 so the output is cleaned for Claude. With no CLI they say nothing was audited and give the install command Claude Desktop {"mcpServers": {"kube-noob": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["--from", "kube-noob==0.11.1", "kube-noob", "mcp"]}}} in its MCP server configuration The MCP server over stdio, every tool claude.ai chat The Agent Skill zip, uploaded under Customize > Skills The tools in claude.ai's code sandbox, offline. The directory plugin's skills load in chat too, but chat has no shell on your machine: they give you the command and read the output you paste Any MCP client The CLI by any method above, then the client pointed at kube-noob mcp The MCP server over stdio, every tool Plain kubectl kubectl-noob on your PATH : kubectl, without krew today, and through krew once the krew-index pull request ( krew/SUBMIT.md ) merges kubectl noob passes every argument to the kube-noob CLI unchanged ( kubectl noob audit -f k8s/ is kube-noob audit -f k8s/ ), and, when kube-noob is not on PATH but uv is, downloads the pinned release through uvx The directory plugin cannot carry the engine itself: the directory accepts Markdown, JSON and images from an organization that is not Verified, and refuses a local MCP server and every other file type. A remote MCP server pointed at your own kube-noob serve would be admissible, and is not shipped; SECURITY.md says why. kubectl, without krew kubectl runs any executable on your PATH named kubectl-<name> as kubectl <name> , so the krew plugin works before it is in krew-index. Download the release asset, check it against the digest in that release's krew manifest, and put the script on your PATH ( ~/.local/bin here; use any directory on yours): curl -fsSLO https://github.com/kube-noob/kube-noob/releases/download/v0.11.1/kubectl-noob-v0.11.1.tar.gz && want=$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kube-noob/kube-noob/v0.11.1/krew/noob.yaml | sed -n 's/^ *sha256: //p') && test -n "$want" && if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "$want kubectl-noob-v0.11.1.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -; else echo "$want kubectl-noob-v0.11.1.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -; fi && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && tar -xzf kubectl-noob-v0.11.1.tar.gz -C ~/.local/bin kube

Every demo runs offline in under a second and never touches your cluster or your saved progress: kube-noob demo --list . kube-noob demo <name> --keep DIR leaves what the demo wrote (its sample input, the bundled examples, any report) in DIR, so the commands it prints run again there. The commands on this page that name examples/... use files that ship inside kube-noob. After a brew, uv or pip install, write them where a command line can name them first: kube-noob examples copy examples kube-noob examples list Running the copy again leaves identical files alone; a file you changed is refused unless you pass --force . On releases without examples copy (from 0.9.3), the README shows a one-line curl of the two files it uses. No AI inside: three ways to use it kube-noob is the rulebook, not the chatbot. Its audit rules, playbooks, docs index and graders give the same answer every time, and they run where you put them. With Claude (plugin in Claude Code or Cowork): ask in your own words and paste YAML, events or logs. Claude calls kube-noob's tools and explains the results. Your conversation goes to Claude as usual; kube-noob sends nothing. With OpenShift Lightspeed or another MCP client : the same tools, served in your cluster ( openshift.md ). That client's model does the talking. With no AI at all : the CLI below. Audits, diagnoses, cited search, lessons and evidence bundles need no model and no network, which suits CI gates and air-gapped clusters. With Claude, from the plugin directory (the kube-noob-skills plugin): the same seven skills with no MCP server and no code in the plugin. Each skill checks for the kube-noob CLI you installed, runs it through Claude's Bash tool on your pasted text in a private folder, and reads the verdict and what was not evaluated from the JSON. Ask "is this production ready for OpenShift 4.20?" with a manifest pasted, and Claude runs kube-noob protocol on it. With no CLI, the skill says nothing was audited and gives the install command, rather than answering from memory as if it had checked. kube-noob ask is the one optional command that uses a model: one you configure, and only a local one under the offline lock. Learner or trainer: practise Kubernetes objects offline You write YAML and get graded feedback straight away. The grader uses the same rules as a production review, and it knows the platform: an SCC rejection on OpenShift, a storage class on ROSA HCP. kube-noob demo learn kube-noob learn tracks kube-noob learn lesson k8s-101-objects kube-noob learn exercise k8s-ex-hardened-deployment kube-noob learn submit k8s-ex-hardened-deployment -f my-answer.yaml The learning guide covers running a class. Developer: ship YAML that passes on OpenShift and ROSA HCP kube-noob demo audit kube-noob audit -f k8s/ --platform openshift --version 4.22 kube-noob fix -f k8s/deployment.yaml --platform openshift -o fixed.yaml kube-noob protocol "deploy orders-api" --blueprint examples/blueprint.yaml kube-noob helm-chart --name orders-api --namespace shop --image quay.io/acme/orders:1.4.2 --platform rosa-hcp -o charts To gate pull requests, run kube-noob audit -f k8s/ --fail-on high in CI. It exits 1 on any HIGH or CRITICAL finding. If you target a Kubernetes or OpenShift minor newer than the one kube-noob's removed-API data was read at, the report says so rather than reporting nothing: $ kube-noob validate -f k8s/ --platform openshift --version 4.25 kube-noob audit | platform=openshift k8s=1.38 | score=100.0 | not checked: The Kubernetes deprecated-API migration guide was read at 1.37, so no removed or deprecated API finding here means none through 1.37 -- not none in 1.38. Check the guide for 1.38 before reading this as clean. In JSON the same thing arrives as a notCheckedBeyond block, and api_history carries checkedThrough and beyondCheckedVersions . A target at or below the ceiling says nothing extra, because for those the answer is complete. When the report is going into a model's context rather than a terminal, add --compact : kube-noob --format json audit -f k8s/ --platform openshift --compact Each rule's constant fields -- title, severity, remediation, citations, controls and the rest -- are collected once into a ruleInfo map keyed by rule id instead of being repeated on every finding that rule produced. On this repository's examples/ directory that is 122 findings over 21 rules, and the JSON goes from 170 266 to 92 330 bytes with nothing dropped: kube_noob.audit.compact.expand_report turns it back into the flat report exactly. The MCP and HTTP tool takes the same thing as compact: true , off by default so the flat shape stays what it was. The exit cod

Writing YAML and getting precise feedback teaches the habits. kube-noob closes that loop offline: Graded by production rules. Exercises are checked by the 60-rule audit engine and the strict schemas that review real manifests. A passing answer is one a platform team would accept. Platform-aware. The same Deployment is right on Kubernetes and wrong on OpenShift (fixed runAsUser against restricted-v2 ) or on ROSA HCP (storage class, Routes). Learners see why. Cited. Lessons and feedback point to credited sources ( [kn:<doc>#<n>] ), so learners know where each rule comes from. No cluster, no cloud bill, no network. It runs on a laptop, in a classroom or on an air-gapped machine. The curriculum has 6 tracks (Kubernetes, OpenShift, ROSA HCP, Helm, RHACS/StackRox), with 22 lessons, 9 graded exercises and 15 quiz questions. Running a class pipx install kube-noob kube-noob learn tracks --learner alice kube-noob learn lesson k8s-101-objects --learner alice kube-noob learn exercise k8s-ex-hardened-deployment kube-noob learn submit k8s-ex-hardened-deployment -f answer.yaml --learner alice kube-noob learn progress --learner alice Each learner earns credits for passing exercises and quizzes. Progress lives in their data directory. A submission exits 0 when it passes, so instructors can grade a folder of answers in a script. In Claude, the tutor prompt runs the same loop conversationally, one concept at a time. Running kube-noob as a shared server for a whole class (one deployment, several learners connecting over HTTP)? Every caller must pass its own learner ; the server refuses the CLI's single-user "local" default so no learner's progress is ever silently shared with another's. Start with kube-noob demo learn to see a full lesson-and-grade cycle in seconds. Mechanism walks: what happens, in order, and where it stops Every other track teaches what to write and what passes. The mechanisms track teaches what happens , in order, along one path -- and grades it against your own manifests, offline: kube-noob learn mechanism mech-net-request-to-pod -f ./manifests Each hop gets one of three answers, and the third is why this exists: holds -- the objects the hop needs are here, and the rules that read them found nothing. The step names those rules, so you can check the claim. BROKEN -- a rule on this hop produced a finding, reported with its id and severity. The walk carries on to the end, because a finding is a verdict. cannot judge -- an object the hop needs is absent, or it is here and nothing could read it. The walk stops. The hops after it are not drawn and are counted as not walked. That last rule is the whole point. A projectcalico.org/v3 NetworkPolicy in the middle of the path is an object kube-noob has no reader for; a walk that continued past it would report the readiness hop as working on a path whose policy hop nobody looked at. So the path's verdict is that no verdict was reached: what the walk did verdict exit every observable hop holds, and at least one hop was judged complete 0 reached the end, a hop is broken broken 1 found a broken hop, then stopped at a hop it could not judge broken , with stoppedAt set 1 stopped at a hop it could not judge, nothing broken before it stopped 5 judged no hop at all stopped 5 every hop it read holds, and the audit of the same input is undetermined stopped , stoppedAt null 5 5 and 1 are not two answers to the same question: 1 says something on the path is wrong, 5 says the path was not walked far enough to say. A broken hop answers the question by itself -- no hop after it can make the path work -- so a walk that finds one and then stops is 1 , with the stop named beside it, not 5 (G400). The network lesson follows the Ingress to its Service. Its second hop asks whether every Service an Ingress backend names is in the namespace, and serves the port the backend names (KN-V024). An Ingress routing to a Service that is not there, or to port 9999 of one that serves 8080, is BROKEN at that hop when a whole namespace was passed; on a fragment the missing Service may be in another file, so the hop says cannot judge . Before this hop existed the walk went from "there is an Ingress" straight to "the Service finds pods", and an Ingress pointing at nothing walked complete (G405). A walk judges one namespace, and names it. A path runs inside a namespace: an Ingress routes to a Service of its own namespace, and a Service selects pods of its own. All three serve the same MCP tools, and all three start offline and read-only. Mode Who calls it Network exposure When to use Service (Helm chart) MCP clients and OpenShift Lightspeed, over HTTP with a bearer token ClusterIP; optional Route One shared instance for a team or the whole cluster Sidecar Only containers in the same pod, on 127.0.0.1 none Your own bot or agent that needs Kubernetes expertise OpenShift Lightspeed tool Lightspeed's chat in the console calls the Service in-cluster only Developers ask in the console; kube-noob supplies audits, diagnoses and cited answers 1. Service mode oc new-project kube-noob oc create secret generic kube-noob-token --from-literal=token="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" helm install kube-noob deploy/helm/kube-noob -n kube-noob --set auth.existingSecret=kube-noob-token --set config.offline=true --set config.defaultPlatform=rosa-hcp oc rollout status deployment/kube-noob -n kube-noob helm test kube-noob -n kube-noob config.offline=true is the admin lock: no web, no corpus downloads, local models only. The pod runs under restricted-v2 . NetworkPolicies allow only the same namespace and the router by default. Egress allows DNS only. Read-only cluster evidence ( cluster_get , cluster_debug_workload ) is opt-in. Set --set config.clusterEnabled=true --set "rbac.namespaces={shop,payments}" and list the API server CIDRs in networkPolicy.egress.apiServerCIDRs . The ServiceAccount gets read verbs only, never Secrets, and by default only in its own namespace plus rbac.namespaces ; rbac.scope=cluster widens that. Every holder of the token reads through this ServiceAccount, so grant only the namespaces its users may see. Over HTTP, tools that write the learning file are not offered, because callers share one file. Add team notes with oc exec deploy/kube-noob -- kube-noob learning note ... (with persistence.enabled=true and replicaCount=1 ). Persist notes, corpus and progress with --set persistence.enabled=true --set replicaCount=1 (a ReadWriteOnce volume attaches to one node, so the chart uses one replica and the Recreate strategy with it). Your own runbooks: kube-noob corpus add-docs <folder> --source platform-runbooks indexes them wherever the CLI or plugin runs. Loading runbooks into the in-cluster service (an init container that reads a Git repo or a ConfigMap) is on the roadmap. Clients connect to http://kube-noob.kube-noob.svc:8080/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <token> . Callers that do not speak MCP (CI jobs, scripts, a chat bot) use the REST routes beside it, with the same token and the same tools: POST /v1/insight , /v1/diagnose , /v1/audit , /v1/known-issues , /v1/policy/reach , /v1/memory/match (with memory.source ), /v1/must-gather (with mustGather.pvc.claimName ), and GET or POST /v1/reports . GET /v1/openapi.json describes them ( docs/api/openapi.json ); GET /v1 lists the routes this install offers. Bodies are JSON objects with the tool's arguments; a POST must be application/json . curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text": "0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory."}' http://kube-noob.kube-noob.svc:8080/v1/diagnose 2. Sidecar mode deploy/sidecar/app-with-kube-noob-sidecar.yaml is a complete example. kube-noob listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 inside your pod, so no Service, Route or token is needed. Your container calls http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp . Audit the example with: kube-noob audit -f deploy/sidecar/app-with-kube-noob-sidecar.yaml --platform openshift --fail-on medium 3. OpenShift Lightspeed integration OpenShift Lightspeed can call external MCP servers when the MCPServer feature gate is on. Lightspeed's own model does the talking; kube-noob answers its tool calls with audits, diagnoses and cited docs, and calls no model itself. The field names below come from the OLSConfig API in the lightspeed-operator. Run oc explain olsconfig.spec.mcpServers to confirm the schema of your installed version. Install kube-noob in service mode (section 1), then let the Lightspeed namespace reach it: helm upgrade kube-noob deploy/helm/kube-noob -n kube-noob --reuse-values --set networkPolicy.allowIngressNamespace=openshift-lightspeed Give Lightspeed the bearer token. The operator reads the header value from the key header of a Secret in its own namespace: oc create secret generic kube-noob-mcp-auth -n openshift-lightspeed --from-literal=header="Bearer $(oc get secret kube-noob-token -n kube-noob -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d)" Register the server and turn on the gate: apiVersion: ols.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: OLSConfig metadata: name: cluster spec: featureGates: - MCPServ

JIRA_EVERY_DAYS=1 runs it daily. A run that cannot decrypt the previous copy fails and does not replace it corpus-refresh.yml Sunday 03:41 UTC Corpus refresh also ingests Git docs and release history corpus-refresh.yml Monday 04:23 CodeQL codeql.yml Monday 06:41 Risk review: dependency CVEs, released-image CVEs, upstream drift, SDK drift risk-review.yml Monday 04:37 US Central (09:37 or 10:37 UTC) Agent review: reads the issue and open Dependabot PRs, verifies facts, fixes, pushes a patch and hands back the tag command Claude scheduled task "kube-noob weekly risk review" Tuesday 03:41 OpenSSF Scorecard scorecard.yml Weekly Dependabot PRs for pip, Actions and the base image dependabot.yml The risk review opens or updates one GitHub issue per ISO week titled Weekly risk review <year>-W<week> with the label risk-review , plus release-needed when a patch release is recommended. It then closes every other open risk-review issue as superseded, so the open list holds the current week only: an open issue is a claim that something wants doing, and a report that has been replaced is not making that claim. The run fails rather than closing anything if it cannot establish this week's issue number, because closing on an unknown number would close the week it had just written. The Red Hat Jira copy: where it lives Ticket text is not on kube-noob.com and is not in the public kube-noob-db image. Red Hat's issue content is not redistributable. The website's known-issues pages are the release-note bugs, which are a different, smaller set. The main copy is the encrypted artifact jira-main-copy-encrypted from the last successful corpus-refresh run. Import it locally (the passphrase is the CORPUS_PASSPHRASE Actions secret, not something to paste into a chat): # after decrypting the artifact to jira-snapshot.tgz with that passphrase kube-noob corpus import jira-snapshot.tgz kube-noob ticket OCPBUGS-1234 kube-noob corpus jira-changes --since 2d A sync only adds or refreshes tickets. It will not write a shard smaller than the one it loaded. The scheduled pull runs every other day, newest updates first ( ORDER BY updated DESC ). Set the repository variable JIRA_EVERY_DAYS to 1 for a daily pull. Do not rotate CORPUS_PASSPHRASE until the current artifact has been re-encrypted with the new value: a mismatch now fails the workflow instead of discarding the copy, and fresh=true is the only way to start over on purpose. When the corpus refresh refuses the copy The privacy audit exits 1 rather than keep a copy that still has person-shaped text in it, which is the right way round. Each finding now reads <TICKET> <field>: <kind> <shape> , where the shape is the match with its content removed -- spelled-out email A at A.A , account id 9A9A9A9 -- so a failure can be triaged from the CI log without decrypting the copy and without the log carrying anyone's details. Two known false-positive shapes, both from patterns that are deliberately broad because missing real personal data is worse than over-matching: account id 9A9A9A9 on a sha256: image digest. BARE_ACCOUNT_ID matches any 24-character hex run starting with 5 , which a digest fragment satisfies. The anonymiser replaces it with <account> , so the ticket text loses a digest; it is not a leak. Do not narrow the pattern to fix the cosmetics. spelled-out email A at A.A on text like "ping Commenter A at quay.io", which is what a labelled commenter name followed by a hostname looks like. anonymise scrubs again after labelling for exactly this reason, so a surviving one means the text reached the audit by another path. A finding whose shape is neither of those is a real leak: fix the anonymiser, do not raise the gate. Risk vectors and the release rule Vector Signal Release? Python dependency CVE with a fix pip-audit on requirements.lock yes, patch Fixable HIGH/CRITICAL CVE in the released image Trivy on ghcr.io/kube-noob/kube-noob:<latest> yes, patch (rebuild) Upstream release newer than verified knowledge Kubernetes, OpenShift, Helm, StackRox vs scripts/risk_baseline.json yes, after re-verifying facts New mcp or anthropic SDK PyPI vs lock pins review; release only if behaviour changes Unfixed CVE (no fix yet) pip-audit / Trivy review, document, no release Procedure Open the latest risk-review issue (or run gh workflow run risk-review.yml ). To bring your own, create a Secret with the key token and set auth.existingSecret ; do this with helm template or GitOps (Argo CD, Flux), where the chart cannot look the Secret up and would rotate the token. Clients connect to http://<release>-kube-noob.<namespace>.svc:8080/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <token> . Secure by default Pods are written for restricted-v2 (arbitrary UID, no capabilities, RuntimeDefault seccomp, read-only root filesystem). The Pod Security restricted half is enforced in CI; restricted-v2 is an OpenShift SCC and every CI cluster is kind, so that half is the pod spec meeting the SCC's requirements rather than an SCC admitting it -- docs/roadmap.md tracks the OpenShift cluster that would close it. NetworkPolicy: ingress only from the same namespace and the OpenShift router; egress to DNS only. No web access, no cluster access and no model calls unless you turn them on. The admission webhook is off unless you set admission.enabled , and denies nothing unless you list a rule in admission.enforce . b: Start Overview Install kube-noob Use cases Learning with kube-noob Run it Run kube-noob on OpenShift and ROSA Operations: weekly risk review and releases kube-noob Helm chart kube-noob plugin Trust Architecture Privacy Security Policy Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 Guidance traceability Release readiness: kube-noob 0.1.0 Third-party notices and attribution Project Roadmap: the ground truth for Kubernetes and OpenShift operations Changelog Demo recordings Corpus, training and the reward Getting kube-noob into OpenShift's catalogs Contributing kube-noob 0.2.0: scope and acceptance criteria More Editions: what is free and what an enterprise edition could hold FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators: what kube-noob's findings are evidence for External ideation, reviewed What kube-noob cannot tell you Open questions, for an external reviewer Shipping kube-noob through Red Hat's distribution channels What kube-noob reads from a cluster, and what the chart grants Red-teaming a change, and ranking what comes out The report needs a coverage ledger, and the renderers should project it Defect classes the adversarial reviews keep finding Safety contract Scorecard Reference MCP tools CLI Audit rules Playbooks Knowledge base Known issues index Helm values kube-noob plugin Kubernetes, OpenShift, ROSA HCP, Helm and RHACS/StackRox expertise as tools for Claude. No AI inside: Claude does the thinking; kube-noob supplies the audit rules, read-only-first troubleshooting steps, cited docs and graded exercises, and runs on your computer. Design and review requests follow a 7-step protocol: Clarify, Validate, Research, Audit, Calibrate, Generate, Red Team. Install In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob /plugin install kube-noob@kube-noob In claude.ai or the Claude desktop app: Customize > Plugins > Add > Add marketplace , enter kube-noob/kube-noob , then add kube-noob from the list. It is saved to your account and also reaches Claude Code. The tools run on your computer, so they work in Claude Code and in Cowork sessions on your computer; in a chat conversation only the skills load. The server needs uv ( brew install uv or pipx install uv ). How to use it Ask Claude in your own words; the skills route the work to kube-noob's tools. "Review this Deployment for OpenShift 4.22" and paste the YAML: findings with line numbers, fixes and the RHACS policy each one would trip. "My pod is in CrashLoopBackOff" and paste oc describe pod or the events: the likely cause, then read-only checks first; anything that changes the cluster comes last and needs your approval. "Write manifests for orders-api on ROSA HCP with shared storage": audited YAML through the 7-step protocol. "Is this a known bug?" with an OpenShift error: the matching issue from the release notes, its link, the version that fixes it and the workaround. "Why was this denied?" with a Kyverno, Gatekeeper, Pod Security, SCC, quota or RBAC error, or "can frontend reach orders-api on 8080?": the policy and rule that decided it, the field that failed and the fix. "Teach me Services" or "give me an exercise": lessons and graded exercises. Commands in an answer are for you to run: the skills tell Claude to hand them to you rather than run them, and kube-noob itself never changes your cluster. How it runs Claude Code starts the server with uv run --frozen --isolated against the readable Python source in server/ , installing the dependencies at the exact versions and SHA-256 hashes in the uv.lock beside this file into a throwaway environment in uv's cache. -I keeps your working directory and PYTHONPATH off sys.path , and -B writes no .pyc into the plugin. If no Python 3.11 or later is present, uv downloads its managed CPython once. Nothing else is downloaded and no LLM SDK is installed. Running the published package from an index instead would be cleared by the directory's automatic checks, where this launcher is held for a human reviewer. kube-noob does not do it, and the reason is worth stating plainly: a launcher that names a package and a version fixes that package, and leaves the rest of the tree to be resolved when the user first runs it. This one resolves nothing. The source is the readable copy in server/ , every dependency is fixed to an exact version and SHA-256 hash in the uv.lock beside this file, and --frozen refuses to re-resolve any of it. The trade is a slower listing for an install that is identical on every machine and auditable before it runs, and that is the right way round for a tool people point at production clusters. The pre-action hook hooks/hooks.json registers a PreToolUse hook on Bash and PowerShell that is off until you turn on verify_cluster_commands in /config . While it is off, the hook is a POSIX sh guard that reads that option from the environment Claude Code gives it and exits at once: it starts no program, uv included (about 2 ms). Turned on, it runs the bundled kube-noob verify through the same uv run launcher as the server, which was measured at 1.5 s per Bash command with uv's cache warm and 2.7 s on the first, cold call; a deny is blocked, a change it cannot decide asks you, and when uv is missing or its run fails the guard itself blocks the command (exit 2, with a one-line reason), on any Claude Code version. The check stops itself at 20 seconds, and the guard kills a uv run that has not finished in 45 and blocks, inside Claude Code's 60-second timeout (which would let the call through). On Windows the guard needs Git Bash: without it, Claude Code runs the hook in PowerShell, where it does not parse, and the check does not run at all (nothing is blocked; this is read from Claude Code's documentation and has not been run on Windows). To have it there, install Git for Windows or use kube-noob hook install from the CLI, which writes a settings entry with "onFailure": "block" for you alone. What the vendored copy is The server source in server/ is the modules of the kube-noob repository 's src/kube_noo

b: Start Overview Install kube-noob Use cases Learning with kube-noob Run it Run kube-noob on OpenShift and ROSA Operations: weekly risk review and releases kube-noob Helm chart kube-noob plugin Trust Architecture Privacy Security Policy Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 Guidance traceability Release readiness: kube-noob 0.1.0 Third-party notices and attribution Project Roadmap: the ground truth for Kubernetes and OpenShift operations Changelog Demo recordings Corpus, training and the reward Getting kube-noob into OpenShift's catalogs Contributing kube-noob 0.2.0: scope and acceptance criteria More Editions: what is free and what an enterprise edition could hold FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators: what kube-noob's findings are evidence for External ideation, reviewed What kube-noob cannot tell you Open questions, for an external reviewer Shipping kube-noob through Red Hat's distribution channels What kube-noob reads from a cluster, and what the chart grants Red-teaming a change, and ranking what comes out The report needs a coverage ledger, and the renderers should project it Defect classes the adversarial reviews keep finding Safety contract Scorecard Reference MCP tools CLI Audit rules Playbooks Knowledge base Known issues index Helm values Architecture kube-noob has no model inside. The server, the CLI and the plugin run deterministic code: rules, schemas, playbooks, a BM25 index and graders. A model appears only on the client side (Claude, Lightspeed, any MCP client) or in the optional kube-noob ask agent, which calls the same toolkit. Request flow (run_protocol) Clarify - platform/version inference (blueprint > explicit > request text > manifest API groups), blocking questions vs stated assumptions. Validate - strict JSON schema (Kubernetes 1.35 + CRDs), apiVersion/kind catalog, removed APIs per target version, selector/port wiring. Research - BM25 over local knowledge; results carry chunk ids, source URLs and licenses. Audit - security, RBAC, network exposure, storage access modes vs provisioner capabilities. Calibrate - probes, resources, replicas, PDBs, topology spread, HPA prerequisites. Generate - deterministic generator (blueprints) or mechanical fixer (existing YAML) with a change log. Red Team - nine adversarial scenarios evaluated on the final output; remaining HIGH/CRITICAL findings mark the result blocked . What the audit says when it did not read something Every reader in the audit engine records a gap in one of five places, and every renderer reads them through one predicate, so a gap can neither hide in a format nor read as a pass (G272, seventh review): AuditContext.cannot_decide(rule_id, why, resource=None) records that a RULE declined on an OBJECT. why is a fixed phrase (never the input's text; the input lives only in resource , cleaned), and Report.declined carries the per-object detail, bounded, per rule. Report.not_audited is the list of {object, kind, why} records that an OBJECT was not audited without a rule declining on it: a pod spec in a kind with no reader, a container image an operator supplies, an object in an API group the reader refuses. why is a fixed phrase. JSON key notAudited . Report.not_evaluated maps a RULE to why it reached no verdict at all: "stage not requested", or "declined on N objects" (the summary of declined ). A rule with a finding on one object and a decline on another is partly evaluated, stays in evaluated_rules , and is listed in controlSummary.partlyEvaluatedRules instead. JSON key notEvaluated . Report.undetermined() is the one predicate: not None exactly when declined or not_audited is non-empty. Then summary.score is null under summary.verdict: undetermined , with the reason beside it as summary.verdictReason , audit and gate exit 1 whatever --fail-on says, the gate is incomplete: true and passed: false with the headline "gate incomplete" (JSON, Markdown, HTML, and in the SARIF as an invocation property plus one note-level result), the MCP tools carry the same dictionary, fix 's after is withheld, and the eval grader marks every finding-derived check ( forbidRules , maxSeverity , schemaValid , minScore ) not evaluated with the reason. A stage the caller did not ask for, and the quiet declines of a partial bundle, are not an unread object. Every renderer prints it once: the text headline ( score=not determined (...) ), JSON and YAML, the SARIF notifications, the HTML and Markdown "Not evaluated in full" section (the "Assumed" label is an allowlist of the assumed-version lines), the gate's verdict, the MCP results and the grader. Trust boundaries MCP clients and model output are untrusted input: every tool validates with Pydantic, YAML is size/alias bounded. Text that came from outside is untrusted on the way out too: kube_noob.sanitize cleans every MCP result (invisible characters, role and tool-call markers, instruction phrases, exfiltrating Markdown) and flags it untrusted . Terminal and file output goes through sanitize.visible and its variants: every CLI text write to stdout and stderr at one boundary in cli.main , the HTML report and the Markdown writers directly. The rule is fixed in sanitize (escapes removed, other controls become a space, format characters removed and marked <U+XXXX> inside an identifier, ZWJ/ZWNJ stay after non-ASCII text), is shared with the MCP cleaner, and does not depend on the interpreter's Unicode table; an AST test refuses a private control-character list anywhere else. The same boundary breaks CI workflow commands (GitHub's ##[ and line-leading :: , Azure's ##vso[ , TeamCity's ##teamcity[ ) with the markers <U+005B> and <U+003A> ( sanitize.CommandGuard ), always; gate --github-annotations is the one deliberate exception. Documents (JSON, YAML, SARIF, the AdmissionReview, the manifests fix and generate print) bypass the text boundary and are escaped losslessly by their encoder, so stdout equals -o ; comment headers kube-noob composes into them are cleaned and broken like text. serve , mcp

b: Start Overview Install kube-noob Use cases Learning with kube-noob Run it Run kube-noob on OpenShift and ROSA Operations: weekly risk review and releases kube-noob Helm chart kube-noob plugin Trust Architecture Privacy Security Policy Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 Guidance traceability Release readiness: kube-noob 0.1.0 Third-party notices and attribution Project Roadmap: the ground truth for Kubernetes and OpenShift operations Changelog Demo recordings Corpus, training and the reward Getting kube-noob into OpenShift's catalogs Contributing kube-noob 0.2.0: scope and acceptance criteria More Editions: what is free and what an enterprise edition could hold FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators: what kube-noob's findings are evidence for External ideation, reviewed What kube-noob cannot tell you Open questions, for an external reviewer Shipping kube-noob through Red Hat's distribution channels What kube-noob reads from a cluster, and what the chart grants Red-teaming a change, and ranking what comes out The report needs a coverage ledger, and the renderers should project it Defect classes the adversarial reviews keep finding Safety contract Scorecard Reference MCP tools CLI Audit rules Playbooks Knowledge base Known issues index Helm values Privacy kube-noob is open-source software that you run yourself: on your computer, in your CI, or in your cluster. The maintainers run no service for it and receive nothing from it. There are no accounts, no telemetry and no analytics. The website's contact and license forms are the one place the maintainer receives data: see The website . There is no AI inside kube-noob. When you use it from Claude, OpenShift Lightspeed or another MCP client, that client and its model do the talking and call kube-noob's tools. What you share in that conversation is handled by that product under its own terms and privacy policy. kube-noob adds no network traffic of its own. What it reads Text you give it: manifests, events, logs, error messages and questions. It processes them in memory to answer; names it finds there (a pod, a Service, a label selector, a namespace) go only into the steps it prints. Its bundled knowledge, and documents you index yourself with kube-noob corpus add-docs . Only if you turn on cluster access: read-only requests to the Kubernetes or OpenShift API of your current kubeconfig context. It never reads Secrets and redacts values that look like credentials. What it stores, on your machine only Everything lives in the data directory: ~/.local/share/kube-noob by default, or KUBE_NOOB_DATA_DIR . File Contents How to remove it progress/<learner>.json Lessons read, exercise and quiz results, points. The learner id is a label you choose (default local ); use a nickname, not an email address. A shared server (service or sidecar, meant for several learners through one deployment) refuses the default and requires each caller's own id, so one person's progress is never silently mixed into another's Delete the file learning.json Your profile (platform, versions, team conventions) and fixes you confirmed (symptom, cause, fix). Notes that contain credentials, logs or manifests are rejected. Counters record rule and playbook ids only, never your text kube-noob learning forget <id> , delete the file, or set learningEnabled: false corpus/ Documents you indexed with corpus add-docs (credentials masked), and public corpus data you built or imported Delete the directory corpus/jira-*.jsonl , jira/ Only after kube-noob corpus jira , jira.sync.enabled or importing a snapshot: the public Red Hat Jira tickets of the chosen projects (title, status, versions, the full description and every comment; comment authors appear only as per-ticket pseudonyms such as Commenter A, their names in the text and their @mentions are replaced by the same pseudonym, other mentions become @user, and emails, phone numbers, account ids and profile links are removed; reporter, assignee and author identities are never stored), the sync state, a search index and jira/changes.jsonl (each ticket's status, resolution and fix-version changes seen by a sync: key, project, type, when, before and after; no text). Public data, not redistributable: kube-noob never publishes it Delete the files corpus/DB_SEED.json , known_issues/ Only after importing the public kube-noob-db bundle ( corpus import , chart db.enabled ): when the bundle was built and the release-note known issues it carried. The bundle itself holds public documentation and release facts only, never Jira data or anything about you; kube-noob downloads nothing for it: your cluster pulls the image you pinned Delete the files A sealed snapshot ( kube-noob corpus seal , <dataDir>/seed/*.tgz.enc , the kube-noob-db-jira image) Only when you make one: a Jira snapshot encrypted with your key (AES-256-GCM). The key lives in your Secret store (chart jira.seed.keySecret , workflow secret JIRA_SEED_KEY ) and never in the image, the chart values or kube-noob's files; the plaintext exists only in a temporary folder next to the data while it is imported. The jira-db-image workflow pushes it only to a repository that refuses anonymous access Delete the image or file; rotate the key A Jira snapshot ( kube-noob corpus jira-snapshot -o <file> , <dataDir>/seed/*.tgz ) Only when you make one: the files above in one owner-only archive, for your other installs to import. It holds Red Hat ticket text: keep it inside your organisation (a private image, bucket or volume). The corpus-refresh workflow uploads it only encrypted with your CORPUS_PASSPHRASE Delete the file Your team memory repository ( memory.paths , chart memory.source ) Entries your team wrote and reviewed ( entries/MEM-<n>.yaml ). kube-noob reads it where it runs and writes only on kube-noob memory init , add , outcome , import and migrate-learning ; it never uploads, bundles, publishes or exports it. memory import reads a ticket export on your machine and keeps no people: assignee, caller

Do not open a public issue. Expect an acknowledgement within 3 business days and a fix or mitigation plan within 30 days for confirmed issues. Supported versions The latest minor release receives security fixes. Default posture kube-noob makes no outbound connections and touches no cluster unless you enable it. This is tested in CI and was verified end to end inside a network namespace with no route (docs/release-readiness.md). With web access enabled it only performs HTTPS GETs to allowlisted documentation domains, refuses non-text content types (archives, binaries, scripts), streams at most web.maxBytes , never writes the content to disk and never executes it. The admin lock ( offline: true / KUBE_NOOB_OFFLINE=1 ) overrides webEnabled , blocks corpus downloads and allows only loopback or in-cluster model endpoints; no later configuration source can lift it. kube-noob doctor reports the effective posture. The local learning file stores only user-confirmed summaries and ids, never logs, manifests or credentials. With alertReports.store the HTTP server keeps an evidence report for each Alertmanager payload posted to POST /v1/alert-reports in its own data directory (owner-only, bounded by count, age and size, never written through a link), built from the payload and local knowledge alone: the receiver reads no cluster, fetches nothing and runs nothing a payload names, and one post gets alertReports.budgetSeconds (30) of work at most, counted from receipt, off the event loop; at most two reports are built at once by the receiver and the MCP tool together, a report slot is taken only once the body has been read and is held only while the report is built, and a post that waits more than 5 s for a slot is answered 503 with Retry-After . Every request body must arrive within 10 s (else 408), so a sender that trickles holds neither a slot nor memory for long. The MCP server's only subprocesses are read-only oc / kubectl calls (argv, no shell) when cluster access is enabled; the maintainer CLI commands corpus build --online and helm-audit run git and helm template locally. The Agent Skill ( skill/kube-noob ) cannot be configured out of this posture: its runner forces the offline lock, web and cluster off and no model on every call, ignoring the config file and KUBE_NOOB_* variables, imports the bundled server source only (it refuses another installed kube-noob), and its tools start no other program and open no connection (a test runs them with both refused). Security design Area Control Network webEnabled: false by default; all outbound HTTP goes through one guarded client; web requests (and every redirect) must be HTTPS to an allowlisted domain. Cluster access Opt-in ( cluster.enabled ), read-only verbs on an allowlist of resources, Secrets never readable, ConfigMap values / sensitive env values / token-like log content redacted, strict argument validation, no shell. A read that failed is never taken for "nothing there" (G279): absence is recognised only in the backend's own words, and a list answer must name its kind, its items and their namespace and be complete. Known limitation: on the in-cluster backend a resource counts as not served when the answer is a 404 whose body is exactly 404 page not found , the API server's own text, but Go reverse proxies (Traefik, kube-rbac-proxy) send the same body, so a proxy in front of the API server that does not route a group reads as that group not being served. HTTP server Refuses to bind non-loopback without a bearer token (constant-time compare, and two Authorization headers are refused rather than resolved last-wins) unless explicitly overridden; DNS-rebinding protection with a Host allowlist; health endpoints are the only unauthenticated paths. The body limit is 1.5 MiB, below the 1,000,000-character argument cap so no valid request is refused, and a body on the public health paths is refused with 405 before it is buffered, so an unauthenticated caller cannot make the server hold memory. The REST routes ( /v1/... ) are behind the same token and body limit, pass the same Host and Origin checks, accept only application/json posts, and exist only for the tools the shared server offers (none that writes). /metrics is inside the same token check unless server.metrics.allowUnauthenticated opens it, answers GET and HEAD only, and carries counters whose every label value comes from a fixed set -- an exception type a caller can provoke collapses to error rather than becoming a new Prometheus label. Input parsing YAML

h: Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 Evidence kube-noob produces Deploying inside a FedRAMP High boundary Not covered yet The 100 audit rules and their controls Sources
b: Start Overview Install kube-noob Use cases Learning with kube-noob Run it Run kube-noob on OpenShift and ROSA Operations: weekly risk review and releases kube-noob Helm chart kube-noob plugin Trust Architecture Privacy Security Policy Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 Guidance traceability Release readiness: kube-noob 0.1.0 Third-party notices and attribution Project Roadmap: the ground truth for Kubernetes and OpenShift operations Changelog Demo recordings Corpus, training and the reward Getting kube-noob into OpenShift's catalogs Contributing kube-noob 0.2.0: scope and acceptance criteria More Editions: what is free and what an enterprise edition could hold FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators: what kube-noob's findings are evidence for External ideation, reviewed What kube-noob cannot tell you Open questions, for an external reviewer Shipping kube-noob through Red Hat's distribution channels What kube-noob reads from a cluster, and what the chart grants Red-teaming a change, and ranking what comes out The report needs a coverage ledger, and the renderers should project it Defect classes the adversarial reviews keep finding Safety contract Scorecard Reference MCP tools CLI Audit rules Playbooks Knowledge base Known issues index Helm values Compliance: FedRAMP High and NIST SP 800-53 kube-noob is software that runs inside your system boundary; it is not a cloud service and holds no FedRAMP authorization of its own. FedRAMP authorizes cloud service offerings, so kube-noob counts as a component of the offering it runs in (for example an OpenShift or ROSA cluster in a FedRAMP High environment), and the controls below are met by how that offering deploys and operates it. This page says what kube-noob gives as evidence, how to deploy it inside a High boundary, and what is not covered yet. Researched 2026-10-27. FedRAMP is changing: the Consolidated Rules for 2026 apply to every authorization from 1 January 2027, and the Vulnerability Detection and Response rules from 7 December 2026 for obtaining and for maintaining a certification, with a grace period to 7 March 2027. 20x Class D (the high-impact class) is not in pilot yet: RFC-0033 proposes the Phase 4 pilot for FY27 Q1 and Q2, with the application window 1-4 December 2026 and a cap of ten participants, and applicants need a CR26-compliant Class C certification first (checked 2026-10-31). Both Rev5 baselines and the 20x Key Security Indicators are written against NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls, which is what kube-noob maps to. Evidence kube-noob produces Evidence Controls it supports How Every audit finding names the NIST SP 800-53 controls it is evidence about; each report has a controlSummary CM-6, CM-7, AC-6, SC-7, SC-8, IA-5(7) and the rest in the table below kube-noob audit -f k8s/ --format json (also over MCP) Changes are validated before they reach the cluster CM-3(2) kube-noob audit in CI (exit 1 on high findings), fix , protocol Posture: what the process can reach, and FIPS mode CM-7, SC-7, SC-13 kube-noob doctor (exit 1 on a contradiction); config_status over MCP Policy denials and NetworkPolicy reachability explained AC-4, SC-7, AC-3 kube-noob policy explain , kube-noob policy reach Signed image and chart, build provenance, image SBOM, hash-pinned dependencies SI-7, SR-4, SR-11, SA-10 Release workflow; verification commands in SECURITY.md Dependency and code scanning, weekly risk review RA-5, SI-2, SA-11 Dependabot, pip-audit , CodeQL, OpenSSF Scorecard, risk-review workflow Each requirement traced to a test SA-11, CA-2 (input) guidance.md Deploying inside a FedRAMP High boundary Control Setting CM-7, SC-7 Chart config.offline=true (no web, no corpus downloads, local models only); keep the chart's NetworkPolicy (DNS-only egress) and add the EgressFirewall on OVN-Kubernetes SC-13 What kube-noob can observe, and what it cannot. kube-noob doctor reads the kernel flag /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled , OpenSSL's own FIPS mode as Python's _hashlib.get_fips_mode() reports it, and the OpenSSL version string ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION , and prints one line. OpenSSL's reading decides: FIPS mode on when OpenSSL reports its FIPS mode on, or when OpenSSL's mode could not be read and the kernel flag is 1 ; FIPS mode off when OpenSSL reports it off, or when OpenSSL's mode could not be read and the kernel flag is 0 ; FIPS mode unknown when neither could be read. A kernel flag of 0 beside OpenSSL on (or 1 beside off ) prints (kernel flag disagrees) after the version string, and fipsNote in JSON says which read decided. sha256 backend names the module this process's SHA-256 comes from: OpenSSL (_hashlib) , or CPython built-in (<module>) -- _sha2 on Python 3.12 and later, _sha256 on 3.11; config_status over MCP carries the same fields. The primitives the code calls, derived from the source by tests/test_fips_claim.py , are SHA-256 and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 through hashlib , an HMAC constant-time compare of the HTTP bearer token, TLS through Python's ssl module (the OpenSSL the interpreter was built against: the system one on the UBI image), AES-256-GCM for sealing a Jira snapshot through the cryptography package, whose wheel carries its own OpenSSL build rather than the system module, UUIDv5 (SHA-1 as an identifier, not a security use) for OSCAL ids and UUIDv4 for a file suffix, and random salts, nonces and approval ids from the kernel's CSPRNG through the secrets module; no MD5 and no custom crypto. CMVP validation is a property of a module, its version and its operating environment: the operator evidences it with the module name, version and certificate number for the OpenSSL that Python and cryptography each load. kube-noob makes no validation claim; FIPS mode on is a reading of two flags, not a validation status (G292) AC-3, AC-6 Live cluster access stays off unless needed; when on it is read-only, namespace-scoped, never reads Secrets and redacts values IA-2, IA-5, AC-2 Put the HTTP service behind the OpenShift OAuth proxy backed by your PIV/CAC

Every developer and SRE then gets answers that are safe, cited and read-only first, about their own clusters, their own runbooks and their own past fixes, so the platform team's ticket queue shrinks. kube-noob has no AI inside: Claude, OpenShift Lightspeed or any MCP client does the talking, and the CLI works with no model at all. Updated 2026-11-03, after 0.7.1. Principles Models are the commodity layer. kube-noob competes on what a model cannot supply: the team's own confirmed fixes, deterministic checks, evidence in seconds, and what the network actually did. The verifier never acts. Probes, server-side dry-runs, ticket writes and the gate are separate tiers, off by default, each action approved by a person. Ship fetchers, not data. Red Hat Jira tickets, customer tickets and team memory stay where they were fetched; they are never bundled, published or exported to datasets. Signals over prose. Alert names, event reasons, condition reasons and error templates are the join key between an error, a known issue and a past fix; text search is the fallback. Land where AI is banned. Disconnected and regulated OpenShift first; every feature also works on ROSA, EKS, AKS, GKE and upstream Kubernetes. A disclosure is not a decision. Every defect found in the 2026-11-03 review had one shape: the information was present and the decision ignored it. controlSummary was computed from a list the exception filter had already emptied; policy reach named ClusterNetworkPolicy under notEvaluated and returned allowed with exit 0; REMOVED_APIS answered "nothing removed" for versions nobody had read; compaction hoisted one finding list and left the other; policy_generate returned 95,000 tokens to a caller that cannot hold them; the weekly review left every superseded week open. In each case a careful human reading the whole output would have seen the caveat, and the gate, the pipeline or the model consuming it would not. So a caveat belongs in the verdict, the exit code or the shape -- the part that is acted on -- and a note beside it is at best a courtesy. When the two disagree, the note is the bug. North star: time from an alert or a must-gather to an evidence pack, offline. Target: 60 seconds. Also tracked: memory hit rate and tickets answered without escalation. Who it serves Who Job to be done What they use today What kube-noob changes App developer When my deploy fails on the shared cluster, find out why without opening a ticket Slack the platform team, search the wiki, paste logs into a public chatbot diagnose and the Lightspeed or Claude tools give the cause and read-only steps, in the company's terms SRE / on-call Get from symptom to evidence fast, without making it worse Personal notes, tribal knowledge Playbooks that read before they change, a redacted evidence bundle , confirmed team notes Platform team Stop answering the same 20 questions; enforce conventions before deploy Docs nobody reads, admission policies that only say "no" Org runbooks indexed and cited, audit in CI, a weekly "top issues" signal Security Allow AI assistants without data leaving the boundary Ban them No model inside kube-noob, offline lock, doctor , no egress, signed images, nothing exported Compliance / GRC Produce evidence an assessor accepts, from a disconnected cluster Screenshots, spreadsheets, a console they cannot export from Findings already named to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls, a coverage record that distinguishes clean from unchecked, and OSCAL a tool can import Status Everything below is in the released code unless the row says otherwise. It is now a port of KubeLearn's player (MIT, credited on the page and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ): your own objects as cards on an isometric cluster floor ( ING shop , SVC orders-api , DEP orders-api ), a marker that flies from one hop's object to the next and leaves the card in its verdict, a caption under the scene, a story column with the hop's whole explanation and its object, rules, verdict and findings, the list of hops, a sequence view, an Events drawer of the evidence, dark and light themes, and an overview that states the path verdict, the exit code and what it means. What the old page guaranteed is unchanged: one self-contained file with no URL in it, the same bytes for the same input, nothing from a manifest as markup, the walk's exit code. What a rule did not judge is still never drawn as passing: a hop no manifest can show is a dashed actor marked "not in any manifest", the hops after a stop are grey and "not walked", and green is used only for a hop that holds. Without JavaScript the page is the whole walk as text. While the walk is on a hop the card it stands on shows that hop's verdict (an earlier break on the same card stays beside it as hop 1 and a cross), a policy the walk only counts is named on its card when a finding names it, and the camera never crops an actor or puts one under the caption. A hop's explanation was capped at 600 characters on this page; it is now whole (G411's rule, one view further). A mechanism lesson names its worked examples (G423). Each walkable lesson carries examples: , the fixture directories (relative to tests/fixtures ) that show it, so a page built from the curriculum finds a new lesson's bundles instead of listing them by hand. A value that is not a plain relative path -- .. , a leading / , an address -- is refused by the walk, and a walk never prints these paths, because the installed package does not have them. A sixth mechanism lesson: Deploy an app (G422). kube-noob learn mechanism mech-cp-deploy-an-app -f ./manifests follows a Deployment from the manifest to a pod that is ready: nothing refused for its identity, API version, selector or limits; requests the scheduler can fit; every ConfigMap, Secret, claim and ServiceAccount a pod names present; images by digest; a readiness probe. The four hops a running cluster decides (admission and storage, the controllers, the scheduler, the kubelet) are marked not checked. A pod that names a Secret the bundle has no kind for stops the walk rather than passing. Measuring first also found that containers: [] is silent everywhere in the audit; it is recorded, not fixed here. A fifth mechanism lesson: a packet meets a NetworkPolicy (G421). kube-noob learn mechanism mech-net-network-policy -f ./manifests follows what decides whether a packet to one of your pods is admitted or dropped -- the namespace has a policy, each policy selects a pod that is here, no ingress rule is open to every source, the selected pods keep a route to DNS -- and marks the two hops no manifest records (which CNI enforces the policy, and the per-packet decision) as not checked. Measuring the rules first found three things nothing reads, and the hops say so rather than hold on them: a workload no policy selects, a rule with ports and no from , and a policy port no container declares. A fourth mechanism lesson: a Pod calls a Service (G420). kube-noob learn mechanism mech-net-pod-calls-a-service -f ./manifests follows a call by name -- the namespace's policy, egress to cluster DNS, the DNS answer, the Service and its ports, the workload, readiness and the ClusterIP translation -- and marks the two hops no manifest records as not checked. Each rule was measured with its object absent before the hop was written. A sixth release video: the walk you can watch. demos/video/stage/videos.json gains walk , rendered by the same pipeline as the other four animated videos -- same brand music bed, same Kokoro narration, same captions, same loudness spec, same 4K master -- and the release matrix renders it with them. None of the others shows kube-noob learn mechanism , and a walk is the one answer here that is easier to watch than to read: mech-net-request-to-pod on three inputs, drawn hop by hop. tests/fixtures/mechanism/complete holds on every hop a manifest can answer for and exits 0, with the hop across the node marked not checked and not counted as passed; tests/fixtures/mechanis

The release workflow renders every tape from the released wheel and attaches the GIFs to the GitHub release, so recordings always match the shipped version. The demos are offline and use a throwaway data directory. vhs demos/diagnose.tape Videos All three are rendered in 4K from real output, with the kube-noob brand music; the walkthrough is also narrated (needs Node with Playwright and Chromium, ffmpeg, and python3 with numpy and kokoro-onnx ): Video Command Source 2-minute walkthrough + YouTube thumbnail demos/video/render.sh <out-dir> kube-noob demo and selftest kube-noob as tools for Claude (MCP), 67 s demos/video/render.sh <out-dir> mcp <session.jsonl> a claude -p --plugin-dir plugin/kube-noob --output-format stream-json --verbose session, with its prompt in <session>.prompt.txt kube-noob as a sidecar on a cluster demos/video/render.sh <out-dir> sidecar <transcript.txt> the transcript scripts/demo_sidecar_kind.sh records in CI (job e2e-kind , OpenShift 4.22 leg) The voice-over, title options and chapters are in youtube-walkthrough.md . Prompts for an AI-generated teaser, sidecar and MCP explainer are in ai-video-prompts.md . Animated videos, no video model The same three scripts, rendered locally in the look of the Grok teaser (navy server room, glass terminal, rocket mascot) with a Kokoro voice-over and the kube-noob brand music. Every terminal line in them comes from a real run, recorded when the video is built rather than typed: demos/video/facts.py recomputes each number and re-records each @name line against the code being built, takes the sidecar lines from the CI transcript and the Claude lines from the recorded session. A release that changes a count changes the video, and tests/test_video_facts.py fails a script that hard-codes one. Lengths below are the released v0.7.1 renders, measured from the attached 1080p copies. A local build of the same script can differ by a second or two, because the voice-over is synthesised at build time. Video Length Attached to releases Command Teaser: no AI inside 32 s yes demos/video/stage/build.sh <out-dir> teaser kube-noob as a sidecar 57 s yes demos/video/stage/build.sh <out-dir> sidecar kube-noob as tools for Claude (MCP) 67 s yes demos/video/stage/build.sh <out-dir> mcp Compliance regimes: FedRAMP, EU AI Act, GDPR 71 s no, local render only python3 demos/video/stage/compliance.py <out-dir> then node demos/video/stage/capture.js <out-dir> Needs python3 with numpy and kokoro-onnx ( pip install kokoro-onnx numpy ), Node with Playwright and Chromium, and ffmpeg. Scenes, captions and voice-over lines are in video/stage/videos.json . The compliance video's script is in its own file, video/stage/compliance.json , because every claim in it names a NIST SP 800-53 control id and videos.json may type no digits. It runs through the same schema, voice, music, caption and loudness path; compliance.py is the voiceover.py step for it. Each claim traces to a file in the repository: FedRAMP wording and the control ids to docs/compliance.md , read-only and never-reads-Secrets to docs/safety-contract.md , the DNS-only chart NetworkPolicy to SECURITY.md , and no accounts / no telemetry / on your machine only to PRIVACY.md . The scene before the end card carries the disclaimer; compliance.py refuses a script without it. Voice and music Voice: Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0), voice af_heart , run locally. The first run downloads the model from GitHub and checks its sha256. Pick another voice with --voice ( af_bella , am_michael , bm_george , ...) or KN_VOICE for render.sh ; --engine piper brings back the earlier Piper voice. Music: generated by video/audio_kit.py : an upbeat business groove in C major at 104 bpm built on the kube-noob motif (C, G, high C), which also plays on every end card. No samples, no licences. Music level: --music-db (or KN_MUSIC_DB for render.sh ) sets the music against the voice: -12 by default, -18 quieter, -6 louder, off for none. Every render keeps voice.wav and music.wav , so the level can change later without rendering the picture again: python3 demos/video/audio_kit.py remix <out-dir>/teaser --music-db -18 --video <out-dir>/teaser/kube-noob-teaser.mp4 Source: demos/README.md

The Jira pull is jittered and rate-limited, keeps no identities, and scrubs emails and account ids. For non-public projects set JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN (sent over HTTPS only). Copyleft, non-commercial, unlicensed and Jira content is redistributable: false : usable for local retrieval and private evaluation, excluded from exports unless you pass --include-restricted . Air-gapped clusters: kube-noob corpus import corpus.tgz (names and checksums are verified before import). The corpus-refresh workflow rebuilds everything weekly in GitHub Actions. Export datasets and grade kube-noob train export --out dataset/ kube-noob train grade --task bench-qa-rwx-gp3 -f answer.md kube-noob train bench --out report.json train export writes sft.jsonl (chat format) and grpo_prompts.jsonl . The held-out benchmark ( src/kube_noob/data/evals/tasks.yaml ) is never exported. Exports contain no LLM-generated labels. The reward (enforcer and credit system) reward = 0.70 * task + 0.20 * credit * task + 0.10 * format - penalties task : manifest answers are graded by the audit engine plus field assertions that encode the task's intent; a failed assertion or forbidden rule caps the task score at 0.4. QA answers need affirmative claims (negated mentions do not count), any known-wrong claim scores 0, and answers under minWords are scaled down. credit : share of [kn:...] citations that exist and support the answer (task-declared docs, top hits for the prompt, or lexical support of the citing sentence). Credit only counts in proportion to correctness. penalties : fabricated citations, refusals, runaway length. Use it with TRL: GRPOTrainer(reward_funcs=[kube_noob.evals.reward.trl_reward], ...) and a task_id dataset column. The eval-only LLM judge ( judge.provider ) is for spot checks; its output is never exported as a label. Serve a fine-tuned model Point the agent at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp, OpenShift AI model serving): llm: provider: openai-compatible baseUrl: http://kube-noob-model.ai.svc:8000/v1 model: kube-noob-8b apiKeyEnv: VLLM_API_KEY apiKeyEnv is the only variable the model client reads for openai-compatible , and there is no fallback: without it the request carries no Authorization header. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is the default for llm.provider: anthropic alone, so pointing baseUrl at a gateway cannot quietly hand that key to a third party. Then compare it with a frontier baseline: install the SDK with pipx install 'kube-noob[ask]' , set llm.provider: anthropic and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , and run kube-noob train bench --out report.json . No model is configured by default. Source: docs/training.md

Researched 2026-10-27; sources at the end. Route Who can submit Effort Where it shows Status for kube-noob OpenShift Helm charts, community Anyone listed in the chart's OWNERS file 1 to 2 days plus a manual review Console Helm catalog, "Community" Ready: chart lints with defaults, has a README, schema and test; released as .tgz and OCI Artifact Hub Anyone Hours artifacthub.io (search, not the console) Ready once the OCI chart is published by a release Community operator (Software Catalog, OLM) Anyone, with DCO sign-off 1 to 2 weeks (Helm-based operator, bundle, file-based catalog) Console Software Catalog Later: only if you want OLM-managed installs Red Hat certification (Partner Connect) Companies Weeks "Certified" badge Later: needs a company account OpenShift AI MCP catalog Curated by Red Hat; no public submission path found n/a OpenShift AI Watch; contact Red Hat when there is traction Red Hat Marketplace Closed on 1 April 2025 n/a n/a Not an option OpenShift Lightspeed has no catalog: a cluster admin adds kube-noob in OLSConfig.spec.mcpServers ( openshift.md ). Submit the Helm chart (community) Tag a release. The release workflow lints and packages the chart, pushes it to oci://ghcr.io/kube-noob/charts , signs it, and attaches kube-noob-<version>.tgz to the GitHub release. Fork openshift-helm-charts/charts and open a first pull request that adds only charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/OWNERS , a copy of deploy/openshift-catalog/OWNERS . Sign off the commit ( git commit -s ). After it merges, open a second pull request that adds charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/<version>/ with the release's kube-noob-<version>.tgz . The pipeline runs chart-verifier with the community profile (helm-lint is the one mandatory check) and then waits for a manual approval. Once merged, the chart is in the index the OpenShift console reads, under Helm charts, source "Community". Commands for steps 2 and 3 (GitHub CLI; replace the version in step 3 with the newest release): gh repo fork openshift-helm-charts/charts --clone=false gh repo clone aashishmahajan/charts ~/openshift-helm-charts -- --depth 1 cd ~/openshift-helm-charts git switch -c kube-noob-owners mkdir -p charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kube-noob/kube-noob/main/deploy/openshift-catalog/OWNERS -o charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/OWNERS git add charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/OWNERS git commit -s -m "Add OWNERS for the kube-noob community chart" git push -u origin kube-noob-owners gh pr create --repo openshift-helm-charts/charts --head aashishmahajan:kube-noob-owners --title "Add OWNERS for the kube-noob community chart" --body "Adds the OWNERS file for the kube-noob community chart (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/kube-noob/kube-noob). The chart follows in a separate pull request." After the OWNERS pull request merges: cd ~/openshift-helm-charts git switch main git pull --ff-only https://github.com/openshift-helm-charts/charts main git switch -c kube-noob-0.11.1 mkdir -p charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/0.11.1 gh release download v0.11.1 --repo kube-noob/kube-noob --pattern "kube-noob-0.11.1.tgz" --dir charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/0.11.1 git add charts/community/kube-noob/kube-noob/0.11.1 git commit -s -m "Add kube-noob 0.11.1 community chart" git push -u origin kube-noob-0.11.1 gh pr create --repo openshift-helm-charts/charts --head aashishmahajan:kube-noob-0.11.1 --title "Add kube-noob 0.11.1 community chart" --body "kube-noob 0.11.1: audit, debugging and learning tools for Kubernetes and OpenShift as an MCP server. Runs under restricted-v2 with NetworkPolicies; signed OCI copy at oci://ghcr.io/kube-noob/charts/kube-noob." To check locally before submitting, run chart-verifier with the community profile on the packaged chart (command in the action items of the release checklist, release-readiness.md ).
