b: Start Install it, then the first five minutes kube-noob is a command-line tool and an MCP server. It calls no model, and by default it makes no network request at all: everything below runs on files you already have. Version 0.11.1, Apache-2.0, Python 3.11.4 or newer. Install Taken from the product's own install page at this build, not retyped here. Homebrew uv pipx Container Claude Code Any MCP client brew tap kube-noob/kube-noob https://github.com/kube-noob/kube-noob brew trust --formula kube-noob/kube-noob/kube-noob brew install kube-noob kube-noob demo --list kube-noob audit -f your-manifests/ --platform openshift --version 4.22 kube-noob insight 'paste anything' kube-noob doctor Copy uv tool install kube-noob Copy pipx install kube-noob Copy podman run --rm ghcr.io/kube-noob/kube-noob:0.11 --version Copy /plugin marketplace add kube-noob/kube-noob /plugin install kube-noob@kube-noob Copy {"mcpServers": {"kube-noob": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["--from", "kube-noob==0.11.1", "kube-noob", "mcp"]}}} Copy Every method installs two commands: kube-noob and its short form noob . The install page has pip-in-a-virtualenv, the Helm chart, the Agent Skill for chat on claude.ai, and what to do when an older install shadows the new one. 1. Get the example files The commands in the README name files under examples/ . They ship inside the package; write them somewhere a command line can name: $ kube-noob examples copy examples It never replaces a file without --force , never writes through a symbolic link, and checks every target before it writes any, so running it twice is safe. kube-noob examples list prints the table below. File What it is for alertmanager-etcd.json an Alertmanager webhook for etcd leader changes (diagnose, insight, memory match) blueprint.yaml an application blueprint for the 7-step protocol (protocol --blueprint) denial-multi.txt one Deployment rejected by five admission systems, each in its own words (policy explain) events-crashloop.txt describe output of a pod killed for memory (diagnose, insight) events-scc.txt events of pods rejected by OpenShift SecurityContextConstraints (diagnose, policy explain) exercise-answer.yaml a first attempt at a graded exercise (learn submit) insecure-deployment.yaml a Deployment that runs on a laptop but not on OpenShift (audit, fix) kube-noob-exceptions.yaml a risk-acceptance list with owners and expiry dates (exceptions check, gate) netpol-admin-tiers.yaml AdminNetworkPolicy, NetworkPolicy and BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy tiers (policy reach) netpol-shop.yaml NetworkPolicies and Deployments for a small shop (policy reach) problems.yaml your own problems as test cases with expected answers (selftest --cases) verify-web.yaml a Deployment a check before an action denies, and `kube-noob fix` clears (verify) 2. Paste an error and read the ten lines you act on Read-only steps first. Anything that runs inside a container or changes the cluster comes last and is labelled as needing approval. --format json or --format yaml gives the whole structured answer to a program. $ kube-noob diagnose -f examples/events-crashloop.txt --platform openshift --version 4.22 DBG-OOM · Container killed for exceeding memory (OOMKilled / exit 137) · confidence 1.0 evidence: signal pod_reason OOMKilled; Reason: OOMKilled; Exit Code: 137 likely cause: Memory limit lower than the working set (JVM/Node heaps sized for the host, not the container). other possible causes: 2 (--format yaml lists them) 1. read-only first: oc describe pod orders-api-7c4b9d6f5-x2lqp -n shop why: Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled oc adm top pod orders-api-7c4b9d6f5-x2lqp -n shop --containers oc get events -A --field-selector reason=OOMKilling 2. change, only after the evidence (needs approval): - Set limits from observed p99 usage plus headroom; keep requests ~= steady-state usage. - JVM: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 (container-aware); Node.js: --max-old-space-size below the limit. (3 proposed changes in all: --format yaml lists every one) caught before deploy by: KN-C004, KN-C005 (kube-noob audit) docs: k8s-resources (kube-noob search) also possible: DBG-CRASHLOOP Container keeps crashing (CrashLoopBackOff) (0.9); DBG-IMAGEPULL Image cannot be pulled (ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull) (0.3). Their steps: --format yaml known issues: not determined: No reported issue in the OpenShift release notes matches this text closely. The index covers OpenShift 4.20, 4.21, 4.22 as of 2026-10-27. exit code 137: killed with SIGKILL - OOMKilled or forced kill after grace period signals: event_reason BackOff, pod_reason CrashLoopBackOff, pod_reason OOMKilled, component kubelet context: ns=shop, pod=orders-api-7c4b9d6f5-x2lqp, name=orders-api-7c4b9d6f5-x2lqp Run the read-only steps first (get, describe, logs, events). Commands that execute in a container or change the cluster are listed separately and require explicit approval. Here they are marked (needs approval). 3. The answer you should distrust, and why it tells you An empty list is the most dangerous output a checker can produce. The reported-issue lookup holds the OpenShift release notes it has, and it says in every format whether your release is one of them, so "no match" and "not checked" are never the same answer. Asked about Coverage What it says --version 4.21.5 determined OpenShift 4.21 is in the index (4.20, 4.21, 4.22 as of 2026-10-27): issues that cannot affect 4.21.5 are left out, so no match means none of its reported issues matches. --version 4.16.20 not-determined Known issues NOT DETERMINED for OpenShift 4.16.20: the index holds the release notes of 4.20, 4.21, 4.22 as of 2026-10-27, and 4.16 is not one of them. No match here does not mean no reported issue. Read the OpenShift 4.16 release notes, or refresh the index (kube-noob corpus known-issues --online). A release the index cannot answer for does not change an exit code: it changes the sentence. The same statement travels with diagnose , insight , the must-gather report and kube-noob gat

b: Blast radius If this workload is compromised, what can it reach? posture scan starts at what is exposed. posture reach starts at the other end: the one workload a scanner just flagged, or the one an incident is about. The answer is five legs -- exposure, token, RBAC, Secrets, node -- and each leg is reached , none , or not determined , with the object and field that prove it. Run on two files, it determines little -- and says so This is examples/insecure-deployment.yaml : one Deployment and one Service. 4 of the five legs come back not determined, because a set of files cannot show the RoleBindings, Services, Routes or Ingresses it leaves out. $ kube-noob posture reach deployment/orders-api -n shop -f examples/ Deployment/shop/orders-api: if compromised, reaches no capability the input shows; exposure not determined; 4 leg(s) not determined exposure not determined no Service, Route, Ingress, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute or VirtualService in these files reaches it; one outside them cannot be ruled out token not determined ServiceAccount/shop/default: spec.serviceAccountName unset, so default; token mounted (automount not turned off) rbac not determined no ClusterRoleBinding is in the input: cluster-wide grants to ServiceAccount/shop/default, including through the groups system:serviceaccounts and system:authenticated, are not known; no RoleBinding is in the input: what RoleBindings grant ServiceAccount/shop/default, in any namespace, is not known secrets not determined the RBAC leg is not determined node none none of: securityContext.privileged; capabilities.add against the audit's dangerous list (ALL, BPF, DAC_OVERRIDE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, LINUX_IMMUTABLE, MAC_ADMIN, MAC_OVERRIDE, NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, PERFMON, SETFCAP, SYSLOG, SYS_ADMIN, SYS_BOOT, SYS_CHROOT, SYS_MODULE, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_RAWIO, SYS_TIME); hostPath volumes; hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC; procMount Unmasked; windowsOptions.hostProcess (pod and container) Deployment/shop/orders-api --uses token of--> ServiceAccount/shop/default spec.serviceAccountName unset, so default; token mounted (automount not turned off) [Deployment/shop/orders-api spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName] not determined: no ClusterRoleBinding is in the input: cluster-wide grants to ServiceAccount/shop/default, including through the groups system:serviceaccounts and system:authenticated, are not known not determined: no RoleBinding is in the input: what RoleBindings grant ServiceAccount/shop/default, in any namespace, is not known not determined: ServiceAccount shop/default is not in the input: whether it turns off automountServiceAccountToken is not known, so the token is assumed mounted, as posture scan assumes limitation: File input: a set of files cannot show the bindings, Services, Routes or Ingresses it leaves out, so 'none' is said only of what the pod spec decides and the answer is not complete. Pass --whole-bundle (whole_bundle) to assert the files are everything that applies to this workload. limitation: NetworkPolicies on the entry edge are not applied: check a path with `kube-noob policy reach`. limitation: Cloud IAM and admission-time mutation are not modelled. limitation: Roles that are not in the input are reported in notRead; cluster-admin, admin, edit, view, system:auth-delegator and kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication-reader stand in by their documented rules, and admin, edit and view aggregate rules the input may not carry. limitation: Exposure is read from Services, OpenShift Routes, Ingresses, Gateway API HTTPRoutes and Istio VirtualServices; other routing objects in files are named in notRead, and a live scan does not list them. limitation: One token per pod is followed: the automounted one, else a projected one, else a mounted token Secret; a token passed in an environment variable or by a CSI driver's tokenRequests is not followed. limitation: hostPort is not a node escape: it opens the pod on the node's network, which is an exposure. limitation: Only the escalation rights the Kubernetes RBAC good-practices page names are ranked. A short named list is known to grant nothing ranked (self and access reviews, token reviews, leases, events, status writes); any other bound resource and verb that is not a plain read is reported as not classified. Leg Verdict Why exposure not determined no Service, Route, Ingress, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute or VirtualService in these files reaches it; one outside them cannot be ruled out token not determined ServiceAccount/shop/default: spec.serviceAccountName unset, so default; token mounted (automount not turned off) rbac not determined no ClusterRoleBinding is in the input: cluster-wide grants to ServiceAccount/shop/default, including through the groups system:serviceaccounts and system:authenticated, are not known; no RoleBinding is in the input: what RoleBindings grant ServiceAccount/shop/default, in any namespace, is not known secrets not determined the RBAC leg is not determined node none none of: securityContext.privileged; capabilities.add against the audit's dangerous list (ALL, BPF, DAC_OVERRIDE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, LINUX_IMMUTABLE, MAC_ADMIN, MAC_OVERRIDE, NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, PERFMON, SETFCAP, SYSLOG, SYS_ADMIN, SYS_BOOT, SYS_CHROOT, SYS_MODULE, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_RAWIO, SYS_TIME); hostPath volumes; hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC; procMount Unmasked; windowsOptions.hostProcess (pod and container) This is the point of the command, not a shortcoming of it. A tool that answered "no RBAC reach" from these two files would be telling you something it cannot know. Assert the files are everything, and the absences become answers --whole-bundle says: these files are the whole bundle that applies to this workload. Now an absence is evidence, and 1 leg remains open. --require-complete exits 5 until the answer is complete, so a pipeline cannot read "not determined" as a pass. $ kube-noob posture reach deployment/orders-api -n shop -f examples/ --whole-bundle Deployment/shop/orders-api: if compromised, reaches no capabi

b: Operators Which operators are installed, and are any of them reported broken? Two questions, the same input: a directory of manifests, a must-gather, or -- when you turn cluster access on -- the cluster itself, read-only, from clusterserviceversions and subscriptions and nothing else. The input Three objects: one operator with its Subscription, and one ClusterServiceVersion whose Subscription is missing. Collect your own with oc get csv,sub,ip,og -A -o yaml > olm.yaml . apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterServiceVersion metadata: name: ptp-operator.v4.21.0 namespace: openshift-ptp spec: version: 4.21.0 status: phase: Succeeded --- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: ptp-operator-subscription namespace: openshift-ptp spec: channel: stable name: ptp-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace installPlanApproval: Automatic status: installedCSV: ptp-operator.v4.21.0 --- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterServiceVersion metadata: name: rhacs-operator.v4.6.0 namespace: rhacs-operator spec: version: 4.6.0 status: phase: Succeeded What OLM installed Package, version, catalog, channel, approval mode, the namespaces it serves and its phase. OLM copies a ClusterServiceVersion into every namespace an operator serves; the copies are folded into one operator, never counted as more installs. $ kube-noob operators inventory -f olm.yaml operator inventory (manifests): partial -- 2 operators from OLM data; 1 operator state(s) not determined counts: 2 operator(s), 2 installed, 0 upgrade pending, 0 awaiting approval, 0 not installed, 0 without a Subscription, 1 not determined, 0 not Succeeded ptp-operator.v4.21.0 package ptp-operator (from the Subscription) version 4.21.0 state installed phase Succeeded namespace openshift-ptp subscription ptp-operator-subscription: catalog redhat-operators in openshift-marketplace, channel stable, approval Automatic evidence: manifest rhacs-operator.v4.6.0 package unknown version 4.6.0 state subscription-not-read phase Succeeded namespace rhacs-operator catalog unknown, channel unknown, approval unknown (not determined) note: Subscriptions were not read for its namespace: catalog, channel and approval are not determined evidence: manifest not read: installplans (not-read, optional: it only adds detail) no InstallPlan in the input, so it was not read not read: operatorgroups (not-read, optional: it only adds detail) no OperatorGroup in the input, so it was not read caveat: 1 operator(s) have a state that could not be determined from the input not covered: Operators installed without OLM (Helm charts, plain manifests, OLM v1 ClusterExtensions) are outside this inventory: it reads operators.coreos.com objects only. The answer opens with a verdict, partial here, not with a count: an input it could not read is named, and an operator whose state it could not determine is reported as such -- never as zero operators. Operators installed without OLM (Helm charts, plain manifests, OLM v1 ClusterExtensions) are outside this inventory: it reads operators.coreos.com objects only. --require-complete exits 5 on anything but a complete answer. What the release notes say about them operators issues is a lookup in the bundled OpenShift release notes -- not a vulnerability scan, and not a gate. The notes key issues by release and text, not by operator or operator version, so the match runs through a table of the names the notes use for each package. $ kube-noob operators issues -f olm.yaml --openshift-version 4.21.5 operator known issues (manifests): partial -- 1 of 2 installed operator(s) were not matched against the release notes; 1 named and 0 only mentioned in the OpenShift 4.21 release notes as of 2026-10-27 (3 open, 5 fixed issue(s)); 0 looked up and named in no issue -- incomplete: the inventory is partial (a release-note lookup, not a vulnerability check) complete: no; all matched: no cluster: OpenShift 4.21.5 (given); searched 4.21 release notes: OpenShift release notes (openshift/openshift-docs), known and fixed issues, OpenShift 4.20, 4.21, 4.22, as of 2026-10-27 counts: 2 operator(s), 2 installed, 1 not matched, 1 named, 0 mentioned, 0 named in no issue, 0 no alias, 1 package unknown, 0 not determined, 0 not installed, 0 catalog unverified, 0 not assessed, 3 open and 5 fixed issue(s) openshift-ptp/ptp-operator.v4.21.0 named: the OpenShift 4.21 release notes name this product in 2 issue(s) and only mention it in 6 more package ptp-operator (from the subscription) version 4.21.0 (spec.version) state installed catalog redhat-operators in openshift-marketplace (red-hat) issues: 3 open, 5 fixed OCPBUGS-62719 [open, mentioned, OpenShift 4.20] listed for OpenShift 4.20; b: Evidence What does a reviewer actually open? Not a console. One file, on a laptop, often with no network: an attachment on a change ticket, or the artefact a pipeline kept. So gate , posture report , posture diff and ksi all take --html and write a single self-contained page -- inline SVG, no script, no stylesheet, nothing fetched -- that prints to paper as it stands. The posture pages carry charts: findings by severity, open findings per control, the five standing buckets, and open against excepted over the snapshots kept. It opens with the number no other scanner prints This is the masthead of a real report, built from examples/insecure-deployment.yaml when this site was built. Above a numbered section 1, "Limits of this examination". The gate failed. 15 findings at --fail-on high for platform openshift . 3 checks never ran because no input was given for them: that is not a pass, and section 1 says what they would have covered. 15 findings · Findings worst is high 3 checks · Not run no input was given for them 0 excepted · Excepted accepted, and still listed Every other scanner reports only what failed. A reader who sees only that number cannot tell a clean cluster from an unexamined one -- so what reached no verdict is a number of its own, beside the findings, not a column in a table thirty rows down. The ksi page counts indicators the same way, including how many have no kube-noob rule behind them at all. $ kube-noob gate -f examples/insecure-deployment.yaml --platform openshift --version 4.22 --html report.html An alert becomes a report before anyone opens a console Point an Alertmanager webhook receiver at POST /v1/alert-reports on the in-cluster service and each notification becomes an evidence report per alert: the signals it carries, the playbook diagnosis, the reported OpenShift bugs for the release the alert's own openshift_version label names, fixes your team confirmed, and the read-only checks to run first. With alertReports.store the server keeps it and on-call reads it back by id. The same report comes from a payload file with no server at all. $ kube-noob alerts report -f examples/alertmanager-etcd.json Alert evidence report: 0 alert(s) verdicts: version: not named by the payload caveats: Every section says what it could not determine -- no version label, a release outside the issues kube-noob carries, no playbook, no team memory repository -- and an alert it recognises nothing in says exactly that instead of looking healthy. The receiver configuration is on the operations page , with the Prometheus metrics, the alert rules and the Grafana dashboard the chart can install. Formats something else already reads SARIF 2.1.0 audit --format sarif and gate --sarif : findings in GitHub code scanning, with the NIST controls on the rules and the blind spots in the same file. OSCAL 1.2.3 audit --oscal and gate --oscal write assessment-results , validated against NIST's own schema in the product's CI. FedRAMP 20x KSI kube-noob ksi projects one audit onto the key security indicators, and reports how many have no kube-noob evidence at all. The crosswalk . Pull-request annotations gate --github-annotations and the Action's annotations input put findings on the diff; nine per kind, and the tenth says how many are not shown. Exceptions are a file, not a flag: an accepted risk carries an owner and an expiry ( --exceptions ), and the report lists what was excepted rather than hiding it. What OLM installed, from manifests or a must-gather, and what the OpenShift release notes say about it. Read it How do you know it is not quietly passing? h: How do you know it is not quietly passing? The false-pass cases One output boundary, and you can see it work The twenty-six classes Test it on your own problems One question each Start here If this pod is compromised, what can it reach? Which operators are installed, and are any reported broken? What does a reviewer actually open?
b: How it is tested How do you know it is not quietly passing? One rule decides most of this project's tests: an absence, an unknown or an unrecognised shape must never read as a pass, a zero, or "complete". Verdicts are three-valued, and what was not read is part of the answer -- in the text view, in JSON and YAML, and in the MCP result alike. 63/63 Self-test, run at this build 4093 Tests in the suite 26 Defect classes the reviews keep finding 8 Tests in test_false_clean.py , over the places below The false-pass cases Four places that reported a clean result without having checked anything. Each is the same shape -- silence read as satisfaction -- and each was found by asking what the output asserts, not what the code does. The 8 tests below hold them, several of them the negative control: the entry has to be absent when the check really did run, or it is noise that trains people to skip it. test_the_gate_says_the_manifest_audit_did_not_run_when_it_had_nothing_to_audit test_the_gate_still_lists_nothing_when_everything_ran test_an_assertion_with_no_recognised_operator_is_refused_not_passed test_an_assertion_that_only_checks_presence_is_still_allowed test_the_shipped_benchmark_assertions_all_carry_a_recognised_operator test_the_jira_scrubber_is_at_least_as_strong_as_the_detector_that_gates_it test_the_scrubber_leaves_ordinary_text_alone test_the_bundle_checks_its_own_size_caps_instead_of_leaving_them_to_the_reader The first of them is why kube-noob gate has a "Not run" section that is never present and empty: a pipeline whose manifest glob stopped matching used to keep passing, exit 0, and print an empty section -- which positively asserts that nothing was left out. One output boundary, and you can see it work Every text kube-noob writes -- stdout and stderr, every command but the three servers -- goes through one place that marks what a reader cannot see and defuses what a CI runner would execute. Always: not only under GITHUB_ACTIONS and not only off a terminal, because a log is replayed and the same input has to give the same bytes. The rows below are real calls into that boundary, made while this page was built. In the input On your screen Why openshift​-etcd openshift<U+200B>-etcd A zero-width space inside a name is marked, never spliced out: two different objects must not print as one. ##[set-output name=result]passed ##<U+005B>set-output name=result]passed A CI runner reads that anywhere in a line. A name in a manifest cannot set a step output. ::error title=gate::All checks passed <U+003A>:error title=gate::All checks passed Nor forge an annotation in the step that printed it. Marked, never removed: a character taken out silently turns two different names into one, which is the bug in the other direction. Azure Pipelines ( ##vso[ ) and TeamCity ( ##teamcity[ ) read theirs anywhere in a line too, and are treated the same. Documents stay lossless -- JSON writes the bracket as \u005b . The twenty-six classes Eleven branches, about thirty read-only adversarial review rounds, about three hundred confirmed defects. Every branch had passed the full gate and had tests; every defect was a shape the author's tests had not tried. The table is in the repository so the next change is tested against it -- and it is the most useful page here if you are deciding whether to build on this. The full document . # Class What it looked like The test shape that holds it 1 A skipped input reads as complete A file that could not be parsed, was empty, was a symlink, was over a size cap, or held no object of the expected kind was dropped and the verdict stayed complete, exit 0; a manifest whose apiVersion key was spelled apiversion was given the answer a CI workflow gets, and a privileged pod passed the gate and was allowed before the apply (G325) Every skip, at every layer, appears in the answer; a fixture per skip reason asserts the verdict is not "complete", and a structural test fails when a new skip reason is added without deciding whether it forbids a verdict 2 Truncation hides the worst item Caps applied in arrival or alphabetical order cut the most severe finding; the summary was computed after the cut Summaries from untruncated data; truncate lowest severity first; the withheld count stated in every format 3 Substring matching on errors or kinds Any error containing "not found" read as "API not installed"; kind matched without its group Match the backend's own whole line; require the group; a foreign kind of the same name is a different kind 4 An unrecognised value reads as the benign default A missing status , an unknown phase, a YAML bool where a string was expected, a scalar where a list was expected → "healthy", "none", "no problem" Unrecognised is not determined, with the field named 5 Duplicates and ordering Two objects with one kind/namespace/name: one picked silently by sort or document order; output differed under shuffle Conflicts flagged; canonical order before analysis; a shuffled-input test asserts identical bytes 6 The caveat exists only in JSON Limitations and not-determined reasons missing from the text view, the diagram, or the sibling command that embeds the result Parity test per format for every caveat field 7 Input-derived strings forge output A newline in a path forged a row; invisible Unicode (U+061C, U+00AD, the tag block, bidi overrides) reached output Every input-derived string through the one output boundary; hidden characters marked, never spliced 8 Docs claim what the code does not do CHANGELOG and guidance stated behaviours later defects contradicted Every doc sentence written after a test holds it; the guidance row cites that test 9 A second source of truth A private copy of a list the audit already owned was a strict subset of it Import the shared one; a test asserts there is one list 10 Tests that fail only in CI Wall-clock ratios on a shared runner; a hostname substring tripping CodeQL; an identifier containing secret reaching print. Recurred as class 21: G263 fixed t

b: Playground kube-noob, running in your browser These are kube-noob's real tools (the same code as the CLI and the MCP server), running in this tab on Pyodide, a build of Python for WebAssembly. No model, no backend, no account: what you paste never leaves your device. The first run downloads the runtime (about 18 MB) from this site, once.

h: Your Claude, kube-noob's tools, in your browser
b: Bring your own AI Your Claude, kube-noob's tools, in your browser kube-noob has no AI inside; this page lets you bring yours. You paste your own Anthropic API key, Claude does the talking, and whenever it needs a fact it calls kube-noob's tools, which run here in this tab. This site has no backend: it never receives your key or your questions. They go from your browser straight to api.anthropic.com , billed to your key. Before you paste a key: create a separate key for this page, in a workspace with a monthly spend limit, and never reuse a key that production systems or teammates depend on. Revoke it in the Claude Console when you are done. The key is kept in memory for this page, or in this tab's session storage only if you tick the box (cleared when the tab closes); it is never written to local storage, cookies or logs. Anthropic API key Model Claude Opus 5.5 Claude Sonnet 5.5 Claude Haiku 5.5 Effort low medium high Keep the key for this tab · Forget key and conversation Your question (paste YAML, events or errors too) Ask Try: My pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 137 on Op... Audit this and tell me what blocks it on OpenShift 4.22: a D... Is 'could not find any suitable subnets for creating the ELB... Explain rule KN-S013 and the NIST controls it maps to.... Refused requests fall back to another Claude model automatically (server-side fallback). Tool calls and their results are shown under each answer.
